current_bottleneck: The clean state-conditioned increment architecture works best on the recent-window frame. Naive all-window scaling improves teacher-forced loss and joint factor dependence but worsens IV free-run quality, indicating nonstationary level/regime mixing and insufficient generic state-dependent scale representation.
last_result_summary: 630a trained the 629a architecture on all 4010 training windows. Validation loss improved to 1.0587, but IV full-suite score fell to 2/11. Surface explosion worsened to 72.5%, conditionality MAE reduction fell to 4.4%, daily-change KS fell to 22/25, level KS fell to 1/25, median-bias pass fell to 5/25, pathwise KS worsened to 0.711, and per-cell q99 tail pass fell to 7/25. Joint-panel dependence improved: factor-factor corr 0.907 and IV-factor corr 0.891, but this does not offset IV free-run damage.
next_step_recommendation: Keep 629a recent-window training as the active base. Implement 631a by adding a generic volatility-state memory feature to the same model: encoded levels, encoded increments, absolute increments, and squared increments. This targets weak turbulent widening/state-dependent scale without IV/factor-specific branches.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 510a, 596a, and 610a all score 5/11. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 629a is now the cleanest native joint learned law by mechanism and joint-panel audit, but its IV full-suite score is only 3/11 because calibration/regime/level-occupancy failures remain.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
